correctness.rationale: For fixed dimension d and u, the holomorphic Hilbert–Schmidt-valued family t↦C_{u+tB(z−u)} has uniform Gaussian-integral bound on |t|≤δ/||B||. Taylor coefficient m has rank at most binomial(d+m−1,m); Cauchy estimates and rank-to-trace-norm inequality sum the m≥2 tail to O(||B||²). The first derivative factors V B^T W with V*V=G_u=I+conjugate(u)u^T and WW*=exp(||u||²)G_u, giving exactly the claimed nonzero singular values. Substitution B=A^n and the leading Jordan binomial term establishes the normalized positive coefficient; ||A^n||² is lower order. The nilpotent and non-unique dominant eigenvalue limits are expressly separated. Inspected VERIFY.py monomial-expansion, derivative Gram and Jordan diagnostics; these do not prove the infinite-dimensional tail.
